title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The System Runbook. Keep it, take The System Schematic, or choose another hand.

options.label: The System Runbook
options.lineage: printed service manuals and field guides
options.thesis: A working system documented like a field manual: numbered procedures, margin notes, and live status stamps.
options.viewport: A deep-green rail and paper workbench: a numbered procedure header, a status stamp, a fixed-baseline 7-day trend plate, and a focus-expanding execution log, with standard tabs and tables below.
options.risk: Manuals can read as static documentation; the live stamps and expanding log must keep it a working tool.

raised.raise: Display scale with a hard grid: the runbook title and section numbers repeat at three sizes, so hierarchy reads before decoration.
Focus expansion: the active execution row lifts and its neighbors recede, so a dense log stays scannable.
Fixed comparison baseline: all seven days share one scale and ground, so the trend is comparable at a glance.
Flat color zoning: each work area owns a solid field separated by a single coastline rule, not scattered accents.

options.label: The System Schematic
options.thesis: The admin surface as a live system schematic: four nodes on one bus, with the numbers and states drawn where they connect.
options.viewport: A blueprint-blue console: a labelled system bus across the overview, users/programs/executions/audit as nodes, a signal-trace 7-day chart, and standard tables in the lower half.
options.risk: The linework can compete with dense admin tables; the build keeps the schematic to the overview header and logon, with standard surfaces for work.

options.label: The Shift Ledger
options.lineage: mainframe operations logs and green-bar reports
options.thesis: The system as a live shift ledger: every run, error and owner action enters the record.
options.viewport: A dark-green rail and a pale green-bar sheet: a shift header with date and status stamps, a run-sheet timeline, ruled KPI totals, and a standard execution table.
options.risk: Retro paper can read as costume; the build uses it as palette and density, not faux perforations everywhere.

options.label: The Course Catalog
options.thesis: The workbench as a registrar's catalog: accounts and programs are records you pull, stamp, and file.
options.viewport: A warm manila rail with tabbed dividers, a registrar header and date stamp, a grid of catalog cards for the key totals, and a dense record table below.
options.risk: The catalog can feel archival and slow; tables must stay dense, standard, and fast.

options.label: The Network Board
options.lineage: transit control rooms and departure boards
options.thesis: The system as a transit board: four lines, live status, and a departure log you can read across the room.
options.viewport: A dark enamel board with a top status strip, a left line rail, a network map of users/programs/executions/audit, a departures-style activity board, and a timetable trend.
options.risk: Transit boards are common; the data must be specific to this system, not a generic metro map.

options.label: The Archive Reader
options.lineage: library microfiche readers and aperture cards
options.thesis: The admin record as an archive reader: scan the index, pull one frame, read it under glass.
options.viewport: A dark reading room with a luminous frame grid, a large selected record under glass, a dense index, and a standard table beneath.
options.risk: Dark, low-contrast nostalgia; legibility and standard controls must win.

options.label: The Rack Elevation
options.lineage: data-center rack elevations and patch panels
options.thesis: The system as a live rack elevation: four work areas as units, each with a status light and a patch line.
options.viewport: A graphite console with a rack-style rail, an elevation of four work areas with LEDs and patch cables, compact KPI readouts, and a standard table below.
options.risk: Infrastructure cosplay; the product is a training simulator, not a data center.

options.label: The System Manifest
options.lineage: SAP operations manifests and validated coupons
options.thesis: Every account, route and run as a validated manifest line: the record and its stamp travel together.
options.viewport: A pale work surface with a navy rail and SAP blue numerals: accounts as a manifest table, programs as a route arc, runs as a stamped ledger, with selected rows in SAP yellow.
options.risk: The manifest grammar can turn standard admin navigation into a costume; the build keeps tabs, tables and status colors unmistakably SAP.
options.case: Chosen by the owner: the manifest reading order, grounded in the live SAP palette. It carries the account, route and run story without changing the standard table task.

options.label: The Signal Field
options.lineage: data-sublime barcode fields and sine lattices
options.thesis: The execution history as a live signal field: dense, honest, and readable at a glance.
options.viewport: A black-and-white data field: a barcode of the last 7 days across the top, a sine trace for duration, and a standard table whose selected row pulls its numbers into focus while the field drops back.
options.risk: Pure black and white can read as an art piece; state colors and a standard table must keep the admin task obvious.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the barcode makes execution volume and errors legible. Loses on audience identification: the art-world field is not the daily language of SAP administrators.

options.label: The Specimen Sheet
options.thesis: The curriculum as a type specimen: one form repeated at every scale, with the pixels left honest.
options.viewport: A specimen wall of display type over dense justified columns, with the same face repeating at five sizes.
options.risk: Pixel display type at admin scale hurts scanning; the world is stronger as a logon poster than a working dashboard.
options.case: Loses both axes: the audience is ABAP practitioners, not type designers, and a specimen layout obscures the task.
options.kept: Display scale with a hard grid, carried into the runbook's section numbers.

options.label: The Program Wall
options.thesis: The program library as a wall of tiles that expands the one you land on.
options.viewport: Rows of fixed-ratio poster tiles under a row heading, the focused tile expanding to reveal metadata while the rest dim.
options.risk: A wall of tiles is a browsing surface, not an administration surface; the admin's job is comparison, not discovery.
options.case: Loses product clarity: users and programs need sortable tables, not poster browsing. Audience identification is partial at best.
options.kept: Focus expansion, carried into the recent-execution log.

options.label: The Seasonal Folio
options.thesis: The system's life stages as five plates on one baseline.
options.viewport: Five fixed-scale plates banded on one shared baseline, captions ranked beneath, with a stage strip for navigation.
options.risk: Seasonal stages do not map cleanly to users, programs, and audit events; the metaphor would be decorative.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity: the system has states, not seasons, and the admin needs live data.
options.kept: Fixed comparison baseline, carried into the 7-day trend plate.

options.label: The System Map
options.thesis: The workbench as a map of flat color lobes, each area opening onto the ground.
options.viewport: One swelling lobe dominating the screen, its coastline running off two edges, with capsule controls and a round live chip.
options.risk: A map turns standard navigation into a spatial puzzle; the admin needs a predictable rail, not a coastline.
options.case: Loses product clarity: the map's spatial grammar fights the admin's tab-and-table task. Audience identification is playful but not specific.
options.kept: Flat color zoning, carried into the runbook's work-area fields.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean admin console and a focused SAP-style logon, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar sidebar-and-cards dashboard and a centered SAP logon card, with no world beyond the product itself.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design; the safe exit, not the engaging one.
